strategy_summary:
This analysis reconstructs the intellectual influence of Otto Neurath on Aaron Benanav's constructive socialist theory. Neurath's sprawling 3.6-million-character corpus is strategically sampled using chapter-level targeting to focus on his 'calculation in kind' and 'socialization' theories, which directly prefigure Benanav’s 'multi-criterial' economic model. The workflow first profiles Benanav's systematic essay collection to identify his core conceptual commitments, then builds a stable thematic inventory of Neurath's work. 

The mapping phase then evaluates how Benanav adopts, adapts, or ignores Neurath’s 'war economy' precedents and 'ISOTYPE' visual sociology. By treating Neurath as the fixed source thinker, the pipeline identifies specific 'Anxiety of Influence' findings—such as Benanav's 'Clinamen' (intentional swerve) from Neurath's administrative economy toward a more decentralized, worker-run model—while ensuring all findings are grounded in the specific source documents that originated the 'socialist calculation' debate.

phases.context_emphasis: Focus on the multi-criterial economy, investment socialization, and the rejection of the profit motive.
phases.rationale: Benanav's essays are systematic and conceptually dense (affinity=0.9). A deep initial profiling of his 'multi-criterial' logic provides the necessary target surface before we look at the Neurathian roots.

phases.context_emphasis: Synthesize themes related to 'calculation in kind', 'economy in kind', and 'total socialisation'.
phases.rationale: Neurath's corpus is massive. We must target the specific chapters on calculation, socialization, and economic planning to build a stable inventory of the ideas Benanav is most likely to be responding to.

phases.context_emphasis: Compare Benanav's 'multi-criterial' approach against Neurath's 'in-kind' calculus.
phases.rationale: Consumes the Benanav target profile (0.5) and the Neurath thematic inventory (1.0). This phase detects where Benanav is 'Neurathian' and where he strategically departs (e.g., modern data matrices vs. historical in-kind calculation).

phases.context_emphasis: Look for 'Clinamen' (swerve) and 'Tessera' (completion) in Benanav's use of Neurath.
phases.rationale: Produces discrete AOI findings. Deep depth is selected to capture the subtle 'sins' of omission regarding Neurath's wartime administrative precedents, which Benanav often sanitizes into democratic planning.

phases.context_emphasis: Summarize the 'Anxiety of Influence' in modern socialist calculation theory.
phases.rationale: Closing report. Synthesizes the full lineage from Neurath's Logical Empiricism/Planning to Benanav's Institutional Design.

recommended_views.rationale: The central surface for this specific AOI objective, presenting themes, engagement, and findings.
Shows the deep structural framework of Benanav's work (Phase 0.5), which is crucial for seeing what he built upon the Neurathian foundation.

estimated_depth_profile: Heavily weighted toward Source Synthesis and Sin Identification to ensure scholarly provenance.

Moves from historical critique of capitalism to constructive proposal for a multi-criterial socialist economy.

Its conceptual density, multi-criterial framework, and normative-institutional architecture make it highly relevant to concept-mapping, argument-structure, and genealogical analytical engines.

book_samples.title: Economic Writings Selections 1904 1945   Otto Neurath   Vienna Circle Collection   2004
book_samples.domain: political economy / philosophy of social science
book_samples.structural_notes: Collected works volume spanning 1904–1945, organized thematically into four parts: ancient/modern economic history, theory of economics and social science, socialisation theory, and economics within unified science. Preceded by a substantial scholarly introduction contextualizing Neurath's economics. Includes editorial and translators' notes; diverse essay formats ranging from historical studies to theoretical interventions.
book_samples.rationale: This is a scholarly edited collection of Otto Neurath's economic writings spanning four decades, covering political economy, philosophy of social science, and socialist planning theory within the Vienna Circle's logical empiricist framework. Its high concept-density (economy in kind, socialisation, unified science) and thematic breadth across historical, normative, and methodological registers make it especially relevant for concept-tracking, genealogical, and argument-mapping engines.

book_samples.title: Empiricism and Sociology   Otto Neurath   Vienna Circle Collection   1973
book_samples.domain: philosophy of science / logical empiricism / sociology of knowledge
book_samples.structural_notes: Collected essays and writings by Otto Neurath, edited posthumously, organized thematically and chronologically. Includes biographical/autobiographical sketches, philosophical essays on empiricism and the unity of science, essays on social science methodology, and writings on visual education (ISOTYPE). Supplemented by editorial apparatus, name index, and series backmatter. The volume spans Neurath's career from early socialist political economy through mature Vienna Circle logical empiricism.
book_samples.rationale: This collected volume of Neurath's writings sits at the intersection of philosophy of science, sociology, and political economy, making it highly relevant to concept tracking, epistemological method detection, and genealogical analysis. As a foundational Vienna Circle text, it is rich in technical epistemological vocabulary and systematic argumentation about the unity of science, empiricism, and social knowledge, while also containing accessible essays on visual education that demonstrate Neurath's broader pragmatic and democratic commitments.

book_samples.title: Modern Man in the Making   Otto Neurath   A. A. Knopf   1939
book_samples.domain: social science / visual statistics / public education
book_samples.structural_notes: Hybrid text-image format combining statistical charts (ISOTYPE pictograms) with short prose passages. Organized thematically around social categories (classes, nations, living conditions, health, race) rather than argumentatively. Foreword explicitly disavows social or economic theory in favor of fact-presentation. Ends with source notes and acknowledgments crediting the ISOTYPE team.
book_samples.rationale: This is Otto Neurath's popular science-education work presenting global social statistics through the ISOTYPE visual language—empirical, comparative, and deliberately atheoretical, making it most relevant as a source of key concepts (visualization epistemology, unified science, social fact presentation) and as a prior work traceable through its methodological and rhetorical influence rather than through formal argumentation.

book_samples.title: Philosophical Papers 1913 1946   Otto Neurath   Vienna Circle Collection   1983
book_samples.structural_notes: Collected essays spanning 1913–1946, edited and translated posthumously. Each chapter corresponds to a distinct paper by Neurath. Preface by Cohen situates the work intellectually. Includes bibliography and name index. Papers range from early critiques of rationalism to mature physicalism and unified science program.
book_samples.rationale: This is a canonical collection of Vienna Circle philosophical papers by Neurath, centrally concerned with epistemology, philosophy of science, physicalism, and unified science, making it highly relevant to concept-tracking, epistemological, and argument-mapping engines. Its essay-collection format spanning three decades invites genealogical and comparative analysis of concept evolution across the logical empiricist tradition.
